title: Congress party plans nationwide marches against alleged electoral roll manipulation
seoTitle: Lucknow march against electoral roll issues

tea.why: The party alleges systematic manipulation of electoral rolls and claims the Election Commission has failed to address these irregularities.
tea.want: The party demands an impartial inquiry into alleged electoral roll manipulation and the protection of citizens' voting rights.
tea.changed: Nov 25: The Congress announced that party president Mallikarjun Kharge will participate in the Samvidhan Raksha March in Lucknow on Nov 26.

summary: The Congress party has announced a series of nationwide protest marches, titled 'Samvidhan Raksha Marches', scheduled for November 26, 2026, to coincide with Constitution Day. The demonstrations aim to protest against what the party describes as 'vote chori' (vote theft) and systematic manipulation of electoral rolls. Party leaders, including general secretary K.C. Venugopal, have alleged that the Election Commission of India has failed to investigate reports of fake entries and the mass deletion of voters across several states. Party president Mallikarjun Kharge is set to lead the march in Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh, while various Pradesh Congress Committees will hold concurrent events across the country. The party claims these actions disproportionately affect marginalized groups, including Dalits, Adivasis, and migrant workers, and has criticized recent legislative changes regarding the appointment of Election Commissioners.
demands: Conduct an impartial inquiry into electoral roll irregularities
Address alleged mass deletion of voters
response: No official response reported in the sources.

updates.text: The Congress announced nationwide marches for November 26 to protest alleged electoral roll manipulation, with Mallikarjun Kharge to attend in Lucknow.
